title: Cousins in Binary Tree II
summary: Given a binary tree's root, replace each node's value with the sum of its cousins' values.
statement: Given a binary tree's root, replace each node's value with the sum of its cousins' values. Two nodes are cousins if they share the same depth but have different parents. Return the modified tree's root.
constraints: The input is a nonempty binary tree.
Replace each node value with the sum of values at the same depth whose parents differ.
Mutate and return the original root.

hints: Process the tree one depth at a time.
Before changing children, compute the sum of all original child values on the next level.
For each parent, subtract the combined original values of its own children from that level sum and assign the result to both children.
All next-level values are read before mutation, and level sum minus one sibling family is exactly the cousin definition.
